newsitem.title: USA: ITT to sell more assets, biggest step ahead.
newsitem.headline: ITT to sell more assets, biggest step ahead.

text.p: ITT Corp took another step Monday in its effort to fend off a $6.5 billion hostile bid from Hilton Hotels Corp by agreeing to sell some hotel assets, but the biggest piece of its defense strategy lies ahead.
Over the next few months, ITT is expected to generate more than $2 billion by selling other assets, including two casinos, a telephone directories business and an educational services unit.
Sources close to ITT said the Desert Inn and Tunica casinos were likely next to be sold for about $400 million.

ITT earlier said it had reached a $200 million pact to sell five Sheraton hotels to FelCor Suite Hotels Inc, owner of 48 Embassy Suites Hotels. Under the plan, ITT will manage the hotels and generate some income from them.

The hotels are significantly smaller than ITT's major Sheraton properties and are considered to be mostly in secondary markets for ITT. The move is expected to enable ITT to focus on properties that generate more income.
"In no way is this a departure from our goal to grow the Sheraton name," ITT spokesman Jim Gallagher said.

Still, the proposed transaction drew fire from Hilton, which said it showed ITT's desire to discourage its offer at all costs. "It's just another sign of a purely entrenched management that is making moves, not toward creating shareholder value, but with an eye toward driving us away," Hilton spokesman Marc Grossman said.
Although the sale of the hotels was "a disturbing signal," Hilton had no plans to revise its bid based on the asset sale, Grossman said.
